headline: A group of news publishers has released a standard for tracking how AI tools use their articles and has invited OpenAI, Google and other AI firms to join an advisory board.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a real industry step, but a proposal with no AI company yet committed.
importance_line: Publishers and journalists could gain data to support licensing claims, but no AI company has publicly agreed to join the advisory board or adopt the standard.
summary: Digiday reports that SPUR, a coalition of publishers including the Guardian, the Financial Times, the BBC and the AP, published a standard for tracking when AI tools retrieve, cite and use publishers' content and for reporting that use back to them. SPUR invited OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and Microsoft to join an advisory board, but Google only said it often engages with SPUR and the others did not respond, so none has publicly agreed.
notes: Single outlet. Digiday corrected its headline to say the companies were invited to the advisory board, not to the standard itself; this entry follows the corrected version. Adoption by AI companies is only proposed.
